contentSummary: Morality is a set of rules and beliefs that distinguish good behaviour from bad behaviour. It deals with the way people should behave towards each other, animals and the environment. A system of morality guides acceptable behaviour, for example, in marriage, while rising and disciplining children and in business transactions. Teaching Module3 Moral, an Immoral and Amoral Person A moral person does what is right, and has a strong sense of what is right and wrong. An immoral person is one who behaves in a way that is not morally acceptable. An amoral person is unconcerned with behaving in a morally acceptable way. The best known example of a moral principle is “the Golden Rule” or ethic of reciprocity. “Do unto others as you would have them do unto you.” Opinions on what is right and what is wrong vary widely among individuals and cultures. Factors influencing these opinions include: cultural norms, personal experiences, religious or spiritual beliefs that shape an individual’s perception of Religious Education right and wrong. Right is typically associated with actions that are ethical, just, and beneficial to others, while wrong is linked to actions that are unethical, unjust, and harmful. Making the distinction between right and wrong is essential for maintaining a harmonious society and upholding moral values. While what is considered right or wrong can vary depending on cultural norms and personal beliefs, the fundamental principles of morality remain constant across different societies. For example, the opinions on abortion vary widely, with some people believing it is morally wrong and others seeing it as necessary right. For example, eating cows is moral in Zambia but immoral in India. This allegedly shows that any act is right or wrong based on the values of the particular culture in which such an act occurs. However, many different cultures do agree on certain universal moral values. For example, virtually all cultures agree that torturing innocent people for fun is always immoral and that helping others in need is always moral. Ultimately, the choice between right and wrong lies in our hands and it is our responsibility to make ethical decisions that align with our values and principles. The consequences of moral and immoral actions can have a profound impact on individuals and society as a whole. Teaching Module5 Moral actions often lead to positive outcomes such as trust, respect, social harmony, fostering of integrity, accountability, responsibility, development and corporation Immoral actions on the other hand can result in guilt and shame, loss of self-respect, strained relationships, community harm, social insecurity, loss of freedom, mental health, legal consequences such as imprisonment, mistrust and destruction of reputation.ACTIVITY 4: Showing ways of applying moral principles in daily living Applying moral principles in daily living involves incorporating ethical values and principles into your thoughts, words and actions. Here are some ways to apply moral principles in daily living: Honesty and Integrity: Practice Honesty: Always tell the truth, even when it’s difficult. This builds a reputation for reliability. Volunteering and community service: contribute to the well-being of your community through volunteering and community service Active Listening and Open communication: Make an effort to understand others‟ perspectives by listening without interruption. Religious Education Empathy and Compassion: Engage in acts of kindness, like helping a neighbor or volunteering, to cultivate empathy in your community. Respect and Tolerance: treat others with respect, even if you disagree with their views or beliefs Forgiveness and reconciliation: practice forgiveness and work towards reconciliation in conflict Environmental Responsibility: take actions to reduce environmental impact and promote sustainability Accountability and responsibility: take ownership of your actions and its consequences Civic participation: Engage in civic duties, such as voting or participating in community service, to fulfill your role as a responsible citizen. Moral dilemma is a situation that requires a choice between two equal alternatives. Therefore, a moral dilemma is a situation where you have to choose between two conflicting moral and behaviour. You cannot choose both behaviour, and inevitably you will fail to keep same aspects of your moral code.ACTIVITY 2: Analysing moral dilemmas Critical thinking involves systematically evaluating moral dilemma by:a) Identifying the conflict: clearly define the competing moral principleb) Gathering information: collect relevant information, facts and perspectives on the situationc) Evaluating consequences: considering the potential outcomes of each optiond) Making a decision: choose the best action that aligns most closely with core values and ethical principles.ExampleSuppose you’re a nurse and discover that a doctor has made a serious medical error that could harm a patient. Do you report the error, potentially damaging the doctor’s Teaching Module9 reputation, or keep quiet to protect the doctor’s career?1. Define the dilemma: Report the error vs. protect the doctor’s reputation.2. Identify stakeholders: Patient, doctor, hospital administration.3. Evaluate principles: Patient safety, honesty, loyalty to colleagues.4. Consider options: Report the error, discuss with the doctor, keep quiet.5. Choose a course of action: Report the error to ensure patient safety.6. Justify decision: Prioritize patient safety and honesty over loyalty to colleagues Morals differ among cultures and can be relative. Therefore, a moral code is dependent upon situation and context in which it is upheld. However, some morals seem to be universally true, for instance, it is wrong to murder or torture another person. Many morals originate from religious and secular (non-religious) sources. Examples of sources of religious and non- religious code are families, friends, school, communities, constitution and religion. We learn about morals from our families, friends, school, community, constitution and religion.In this sub topic, you will discuss the sources of religious moral codes, identify secular sources of moral codes and evaluate religious and secular moral codes. Religious texts are an important source of moral codes. The moral teachings of the religious texts of Christianity, Islam and Hinduism are:Christian religious text Christians believe that morals come from God or Jesus his messenger on earth. They are revealed to us through the scriptures of the Bible. The Ten Commandments are a moral code found in the Old Testament according to Exodus 20:1-17. These were revealed to Moses by God. The New Testament contains moral teachings given by Jesus and his followers to the early Christians. Rom. 13:1-7, 8-14.Hindu religious textThe Hindu religious texts include the Bhagavad Gita, the Vedas and the Upanishads. Each of these contributes to the Hindu understanding of morality. The Bhagavad Gita (the song of the Bhagavan) often commonly called the Gita is a 700 verse poem that is part of an epic known as the Mahabharata. It was written between 400BC and 400CE. The poem tells the story of the Pandava prince, Arjuna, who is in a battle against his father. He turns to his Lord Krishna, who drives his chariot, for help and wisdom. This is a very important poem in Hindu moral life. The battle field is interpreted as a metaphor for the spiritual and moral struggles that people have. It shows how our choices have consequences for ourselves and others. The Bhagavad Gita influenced the thinking of many visionaries in the 20th century including Dr Martin Luther King and Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhi called the Gita “his spiritual dictionary”.The Vedas The Vedas (meaning knowledge in Sanskrit) are a collection of many texts which come from ancient India. They are thought to be created by the Hindu god who created the Teachi

competencies: SAnalytical Thinking Analyse central teachings on making choices in the four religions in Zambia.Citizenship Explain responsibility for one’s choicesEntrepreneurship Develop talent to promote entrepreneurshipFinancial Education Apply financial literacy in order to develop the talent.Hook“Your talent
contentSummary: There are three important steps that we need to follow in making good choices. See: we need to use our five senses to identify our options. Look at each option and think about it. Judge: In life, there are some things that are important (for example, passing an exam, playing a game, or starting a friendship). Look at the advantages and disadvantages of each option. Evaluate the options and make the best choice according to interests, beliefs and also time that you have. Act: You take action according to what you saw and judged as the best thing to choose. Chosen circumstances are situations in life that you choose, e.g. the type of clothes you wear, friends you play with, food you eat. Un-chosen circumstances are situations in life that cannot be chosen, they are beyond your control e.g. your gender, parents, nationality.ACTIVITY 3: Identifying the different levels of choices Learning EnvironmentArtificial: Indoor activity Teaching Module17 Group work and presentations of findings Discussions on levels and factors that influence choicesACTIVITY PROCESSTask 1 Learners in groups to discuss the different levels at which people make choices Groups to report their findings to the class Teacher to summarise the information on the boardTask 2 Learners in groups to identify factors that influence the decision making at any level. Groups to report their findings to the class Teacher to summarise the information on the board There are different levels of choices which include the following: Individual level – making a choice for oneself, taking into consideration your needs and what to do in order to achieve them. Family level – decisions made here have more than one person’s input because the choice has to take into consideration the family’s common goals and what is best for the whole family. Community level – at this level, many people are involved in making the choice; so a lot of people will be part of the decision making process.There are many factors that influence choices. They include the following: age, gender, past experiences, level of commitment, existing beliefs, status in society, cognitive biases.ACTIVITY 4: Role playing acceptance of responsibility of our choices Responsibility is the duty to behave the right way or to do the right thing.  It is important to accept responsibility of our choices whether good or bad. The choices that people make show one’s aim in life (the type of friends you have, the way you use your free time, the way you treat people and even the way react when you are criticized) People should be confident and assertive in fulfilling their aims through the choices they make. The following are the steps involved in decision making: See - examine the situation, identify the main problem Judge - decide what it is that you want to achieve, discuss what the most important area is, look at different options, decide what to do, decide how to do it Act- put the decision and plan into actionACTIVITY 2: Evaluating decision making in real life The steps needed in decision making include the following: Examine the situation Decide what it is that you want to achieve Identify the main problem Discuss what the most important area is Look at different options Decide what to do Decide how to do it Put the plan into actionAll the steps are necessarily and important in arriving at a good decision and action in real, everyday life. Failure to follow these steps may lead to bad decisions that will affect individual, family and community life negatively. The teachings of a religion guide its followers in their daily choices. These teachings are important because they inspire people to look at their current life and the future with hope. People are expected to align or position their choices in line with the teachings of their religion. Therefore, people’s religious beliefs and values greatly influence their choices. In this sub-topic, we will look at what the four main religions in Zambia teach their followers to remember when making choices. The central teachings of the four main religions for followers to remember when making choices are as follows:ChristianityChristianity teaches that follower must love God and neighbour (Mark 12:30-31). ‘Neighbour’ means your fellow man. Loving God means putting Him first in your life. This means that a Christian must use his or her time, money and other available resources in a way that pleases God.HinduismThe main aim of a Hindu is to be free from all selfishness. This is because Hindus believe that sin and suffering come about from people’s evil desires. The Bhagavad Gita says: ‘The person who gives up all desires without thinking ‘mine’ or ‘I’ is the one who gains peace.’’ Teaching Module21 Islam The main aim of a Muslim is to show complete obedience to Allah and to live at peace with every Muslim in the world. Muslims show complete obedience to Allah by following the Five Pillars of Islam (declare there is no god except God, and Muhammad is God’s messenger, pray five times in a day, fast during the month of Ramadan, give money to the poor or charity and travel to Mecca at least once in a life time – pilgrimage). By supporting each other in life, Muslims show that they are united and are at peace with other Muslims.Zambia Traditional ReligionThe main aim in the life of a follower of Zambian Traditional Religion is to show respect to fellow human beings and to be at peace with the spirits of the dead. Traditionalists are expected to show love to all people. In order to be at peace with the spirits of the ancestors, followers are expected to: give dead community members a decent burial, name children after their dead relatives, look after surviving members of their extended families, especially orphans, the aged and those who are differently able bodied and give gifts and offerings to the spirits of the dead.ACTIVITY 2: Evaluating central teachings of the four religions in Zambia on making choices Christianity The central teaching of Christianity is to love God and your neighbor. This means all the choices a Christian makes should be in line with this teaching. Making choices in line with this teaching helps a Christian to be at peace with God and man to make progress in his or her life.Zambia Traditional Religion The main aim of a Zambian Traditionalist is to be at peace with the spirits of the ancestors and show respect to fellow human beings. Therefore, a traditionalist should make his or her choices in line with this teaching. Doing so helps him or her to live a harmonious life with other members of society and remain faithful to his or her culture and traditions. Religious Education Hinduism The main aim of a Hindu is to be free from all selfishness. This is because Hindus believe that sin and suffering come about from people’s evil desires. So Hindus should make choices according to this teaching. Making choices in line with this teaching helps a Hindu to be at peace with Brahman and man to make progress in his or her lifeIslam The main aim of a Muslim is to show complete obedience to Allah and to live at peace with every Muslim in the world. So a Muslim should make his or her choices according to this teaching. Doing so helps him or her to succeed in their life.Expected Standard: Central teachings on making choices on the four religions analysed accordingly

contentSummary: We all have different talents and abilities, some of which we are born with while others are acquired through practice and experience. No matter what our talent is, it is important to develop it and use it to the best of our abilities. A talent is the natural ability to do something well. Everybody is good at something, but that something or talent needs to be discovered. For example, one person may have a talent for long distance running while another may have a talent for Mathematics. People have to try out many things in order to discover their special talentsIn this sub-topic, we will discuss talents and how they can be discovered, developed and used to earn a living. A talent is the natural ability to do something well. It is a special ability to do something well, chosen by an individual or developed by regular practice On the other hand, a gift is a more general, spiritual, inherent capacity or abilityACTIVITY 2: Exploring how one can discover a talent One can discover a talent by trying different things. Through their observations and encouragements, friends, family members and teachers can also help a person to discover his or her talents. Talents can be developed through regular practice. Good attitudes such as discipline, self-motivation and hard work are needed if one is to develop their talent Encouragement by friends, family and coaches is also important in the developing of talents.ACTIVITY 4: Demonstrating how one can lose a talent God has given everyone talents according to their ability. The Parable of Talents in Matthew 25:14-30 teaches that people should use their talents wisely because whatever talent they do not use will be lost The talent a person possesses should be used for their own and other people’s benefit A well-developed talent can be a source of earning a living or income. There are many examples of talents that can be developed into income earning ventures e.g. tailoring, hair dressing, dancing, sports e.tc. All talents can be developed into entrepreneurial ventures. For example, a person good at cooking can develop this talent into a catering business; a footballer can develop the talent into professional football etc. By developing talent into an entrepreneurial venture, a person not only earns a living but also employs other people. Developing talent into an entrepreneurial activity is one way of poverty reduction in society. However, for a talent to be developed into an entrepreneurship, a lot of skills and knowledge is required such as financial literacy, collaboration, consultation and availability. One also requires attitude of hard work, financial discipline, patience and inner motivation to keep on doing the work.
